subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: detects people without requiring them to carry or press anything.

subsystems.name: Edge compute
subsystems.role: processes sensor data inside the building so raw video or radar never has to leave it.

subsystems.name: Fusion and tracking
subsystems.role: turns many noisy readings into one picture of who is where and what they are doing.

subsystems.name: Spatial reasoning and orchestration
subsystems.role: decides what the space should do next, based on context rather than fixed rules.

subsystems.name: Actuation layer
subsystems.role: carries out the decision in the physical world.
parts: door locks, alerts and nurse-call messages

subsystems.name: Consent and identity
subsystems.role: keeps the system accountable and legally usable.

buildSteps.title: Define the space and its jobs
buildSteps.detail: Write down concrete goals — for example 'detect a fall within 30 seconds' or 'light the corridor at 20 lux when someone gets up at night' — and the failure modes that would be dangerous.

buildSteps.title: Map and instrument the building
buildSteps.detail: Survey rooms in metres and place radar or sensor nodes so each covers its zone with overlap; avoid blind spots behind furniture and confirm coverage with test walks.

buildSteps.title: Set up identity and consent
buildSteps.detail: Enrol residents or occupants, define who may be tracked, mark private areas as sensing-free, and keep the consent record with the deployment.

buildSteps.title: Build the spatial model
buildSteps.detail: Register every sensor, light and valve with its room and capabilities so the software knows what exists and what it can control.

buildSteps.title: Fuse the sensor streams
buildSteps.detail: Run local inference to convert radar and camera data into anonymised tracks, then merge tracks across rooms, filtering pets, fans and door swings that cause false alarms.

buildSteps.title: Tune activity and intent models
buildSteps.detail: Train or configure classifiers for the activities that matter — sleeping, cooking, wandering, collapse — and set thresholds against measurements from the actual building, not a lab.

buildSteps.title: Wire the control loop
buildSteps.detail: Connect decisions to actuators with hard safety limits, rate limits and a human override, so a wrong inference cannot lock a door or cut heating in winter.

buildSteps.title: Pilot and validate
buildSteps.detail: Run for weeks alongside staff or residents, counting missed detections and false alerts and adjusting until the system is quieter than the people it is meant to help.

buildSteps.title: Operate, update and audit
buildSteps.detail: Push model updates carefully, watch for drift when furniture or habits change, and re-check privacy settings on a schedule.

prerequisites.tech: Low-power ultra-wideband and millimetre-wave radar chips
prerequisites.why: they detect breathing, presence and falls through clothing and darkness without a camera image.
continuous vision and radar inference must run locally to be affordable and privacy-preserving.
lights, thermostats and locks from different makers must be controllable from one logic layer.
accuracy in cluttered real homes is still well below what clinical use demands.
a planner that can hallucinate a room must be bounded by verified rules before it is trusted with safety.

prerequisites.tech: Privacy law and medical-device certification for sensing homes
prerequisites.why: continuous monitoring of vulnerable people raises consent and approval questions that are still being settled.

pathway.milestone: room-level occupancy sensing in smart homes and radar-based fall detection sold as consumer and care products
pathway.unlocks: automatic lighting, heating and basic alerts without cameras.

pathway.milestone: multimodal fusion giving person-level tracking with on-device processing and clear consent
pathway.unlocks: night-time monitoring and early warning of deterioration in care homes.
occupants describing desired behaviour in words instead of programming rules, with adaptation to individual habits.

pathway.milestone: certified ambient assisted living integrated with clinical records
pathway.unlocks: people staying in their own homes longer, and hospitals monitoring recovery remotely.

pathway.milestone: buildings that anticipate intent as a standard design layer
pathway.unlocks: energy savings and accessibility built into new construction rather than retrofitted.
